scenarios.title: Chennai
scenarios.headline: A signal fails south of Tambaram. Trains stop on one track. The promised buses never come.

what.x: Egmore works cut Beach-Tambaram-Chengalpattu EMU services from 204 to 164 a day until 5 April.
Signal failure between Perungalathur and Irumbuliyur. Several EMUs halt on the same track, Chennai-bound, from Chengalpattu and Guduvanchery.
Trains stay stationary for over an hour. Office-goers, factory workers and students climb down and walk along the tracks to Tambaram.
Limited onward services. Special buses were announced, but commuters say they did not run at the promised frequency.
Fault rectified; services restored gradually.

why.x: Tambaram's footfall (about 1.5 lakh a day) now exceeds MGR Central's, but its infrastructure lags: platforms and a foot-over-bridge still under construction.
With services already cut from 204 to 164, every train ran fuller, so one failure stranded more people at once.
Nobody told stranded riders what would move next or when. People self-evacuated along live tracks.
Bus bridging was improvised. Internationally, agencies rarely keep bus reserves for bridging, so buses arrive late and in the wrong place.
Everyone opens a cab app at once: per-car surge rises (capped at 2x base fare in India since July 2025) while 40 people going the same way book 40 cabs.

omni: Detect the halt, count who is affected, and split them into 5 real northbound corridors by destination.
Bridging buses get capacity-exact passes, so nobody is turned away at a door.

Koottu shared cabs: riders going the same way, inside their trusted circle, are grouped at geofenced pickup gates. Four phones compare four quotes and the cheapest books. Surge is charged per car, so sharing is cheaper than riding alone at the normal fare, and nobody is ever charged more than their solo fare (checked directly, not just by Shapley).
Wheelchair users, flight and shift deadlines go first, with an explanation on every pass.
Everything runs on the station edge node, with no internet needed.

Geofence: phones and delivery partners inside 2 km of the station get the alert. Two-wheeler partners take urgent solo riders (where state law allows) and drop water and food to anyone waiting over 45 minutes.

N.how: 3 halted 12-car EMUs (T4, 'several') x 3,504 design capacity (T2) x 0.6 peak load (T4) x 0.3 who walk to Tambaram for road options (T4, 'hundreds walked')

scenarios.title: New Delhi
scenarios.headline: Maha Kumbh rush meets delayed trains and confusing announcements. 18 people die on FOB-3 stairs.
scenarios.memorial: In memory of the 18 people who died on 15 February 2025.

what.x: About 2,600 extra general tickets sold at New Delhi in two hours; around 1,500 general tickets an hour overall.
15 trains delayed. The Swatantrata Senani Express (sched. 21:15, Prayagraj-bound) ran over 3 hours late.
Crowds build around platforms 12 to 16.
Two trains with near-identical names (Prayagraj Express, Prayagraj Special); people move between platforms 14 and 16 over the foot-over-bridge.
Crush on FOB-3 stairs to platforms 14/15. The inquiry cites a person with a large headload falling.

why.x: General (unreserved) tickets are sold with no link to seats, so the crowd grew with every hour of delay while trains ran late.
Similar train names and platform information caused movement between platforms at the worst moment.
Stairs of a foot-over-bridge became the only path between platforms; a single fall propagated through the crowd.
Above about 2.17 persons per square metre, forces chain through bodies; people cannot step back.
Afterwards Railways announced holding areas at 60 high-footfall stations so passengers reach platforms by departure.

omni: Capacity-aware boarding windows for unreserved passengers: a pass exists only if a seat or standing slot exists on that train.
Holding area with countdowns instead of a platform crowd; release in coach-sized batches.
One source of truth for platform information, signed and readable offline.
FOB density alerts before LOS E, with staged release.

scenarios.title: Mumbai
scenarios.headline: Heavy rain floods tracks. Central Railway suspends CSMT-Thane. Thousands stranded across stations.

what.x: Heavy rain. Central Railway suspends Main and Harbour line services between CSMT and Thane until further notice.
Trains stuck between Vidyavihar and Thane; massive crowds at CSMT, Byculla, Dadar, Kurla and Ghatkopar.
Services resume gradually the next morning.

why.x: Mumbai's storm drains handle about 25 mm of rain per hour at low tide; most outfalls sit below sea level and only 3 of 45 have floodgates.
A plan to double drain capacity to 50 mm per hour (BRIMSTOWAD) has been pending for years.
Central Railway carries about 38.7 lakh riders a day; stations and foot-over-bridges were never sized for a whole line stopping at once. At Elphinstone Road a 2.4 m FOB killed 23 people in 2017.
When a line stops, people wait on platforms and stairs because nobody tells them where else is safe or what will move.

omni: Staging: tell people where to wait safely, not just when trains return.
Multimodal fallback by corridor: BEST buses, Metro Line 1 at Ghatkopar, shared cabs.
Koottu groups cab riders by direction so 4 people take 1 car on flooded roads.
Offline passes when mobile networks choke.

Geofence: phones and delivery partners inside 2 km of the station get the alert. Two-wheeler partners take urgent solo riders (where state law allows) and drop water and food to anyone waiting over 45 minutes.

N.how: no station-level count published; Central Railway averages 38.7 lakh riders a day (T1)

scenarios.title: Singapore
scenarios.headline: A faulty train damages track and power on the East-West Line. No trains Jurong East to Buona Vista for six days.

what.x: Faulty train damages track and power infrastructure between Jurong East and Buona Vista.
Free regular buses activated within about five minutes; bridging buses running by about 09:50.
Bridging buses grow from 39 before the peak to 70 by the evening peak. Queues at Buona Vista take over 30 minutes; the Jurong East bridging point is about an 8-minute walk away.
About 358,000 affected on day 1 and over 2.1 million by 30 Sep. Service resumes 1 Oct.
LTA finds degraded axle-box grease most likely caused the failure; SMRT fined S$2.4m (cut from S$3m).

why.x: The overhaul interval for the faulty train had been extended without a detailed engineering and risk assessment.
The bridging point at Jurong East was placed about 8 minutes' walk from the station for traffic safety, adding walking and confusion.
Commuters were confused between shuttle trains, bridging buses and free regular buses; operators later reviewed bridging management.
Bus supply ramps up over hours while demand arrives in minutes.

omni: Corridor-aware bridging: stopping vs express buses sized to real demand.
Unaffected rail (North-South Line) offered as an alternative with honest travel times.
Constraint 3 stage: the bus feed changes shape mid-incident and the adapter keeps every seat count correct.

scenarios.title: Madrid
scenarios.headline: At 12:33 the Iberian grid collapses. Trains stop, the metro is evacuated, phones barely work.

what.x: Continental Spain and Portugal lose power.
Renfe halts trains nationwide; Madrid metro evacuated; about 35,000 rail passengers stranded across Spain.
Mobile networks degrade: Vodafone Spain at about 70% capacity.
EMT reinforces lines 203, 101 and 200 to pick up at Atocha and Chamartin; 11 trains still await evacuation late at night.
Atocha stays open overnight as a shelter; crowds wait for hours.

why.x: ENTSO-E's final report: an uncontrolled voltage rise and loss of voltage control, with generators below required reactive-power set points.
Every digital layer (apps, ticketing, cloud dispatch) depends on power and mobile data. When both go, cloud-only coordination stops completely.
Without phones, stranded travellers rely on rumour and staff shouting.

omni: Constraint 1 stage: the internet is cut at 12:33 and RAHA keeps allocating on the station edge node (UPS).
Passes are signed and verified on driver handhelds with zero network.
A cloud-only coordinator, by contrast, collapses into free-for-all the moment the network goes.

N.how: no Atocha-specific count; about 35,000 rail passengers stranded Spain-wide (T1)

story.lift: Monday 28 April 2025, 12:33 CEST. The Iberian grid collapses. Atocha goes dark.
story.asIs: As it happened: no trains, a weak phone signal, a crowd and no plan.
story.split: Left: a cloud-only coordinator, cut off with the internet. Right: RAHA on the station edge node.
story.omni: External requests: zero. Passes keep verifying, seats keep matching, the urgent keep going first.

business.thesis: RAHA is free for riders and paid for by the operators who carry the legal and reputational cost of a stranded station. The simulation is part of the product: operators use it to size bridging reserves and holding areas before an incident, and the same engine runs live during one.

streams.why: Railways is already funding holding areas and AI monitoring at 76 stations; RAHA is the capacity-linked release and bridging layer on top. Pender et al. found few agencies keep bus reserves: RAHA's drills size them.
Trusted circles (Zimride's model, which became Lyft) for students and shift workers: guaranteed rides home when the network fails, cheaper than solo cabs.
Idle partners inside the geofence get paid trips (urgent riders, essentials drops) exactly when demand spikes.
Capacity-linked boarding windows and holding-area countdowns for planned surges like the one at New Delhi.

business.gtm: Pilot at Chennai (Tambaram station) with Southern Railway Chennai Division and MTC via SRMIST (riders, data and a live corridor next door), then the 76 holding-area stations. Riders adopt Koottu for free because sharing is cheaper than riding alone during surge.

proof.x: Transit software sold to governments is a real market: Via listed at about $3.5bn with over 90% of revenue from public agencies.
Indian state transport buys digital services: Chalo works with TNSTC, DTC and KSRTC.
Station crowd tools are tendered today: one division's information-board tender alone is about Rs 2.13 cr.

business.risks: Long public-sector sales cycles; two-wheeler and multi-stop pooling rules vary by state; RAHA cannot switch surge off, only make it hurt less; fare quotes are entered by riders, never scraped.

constraints.title: No internet, no third-party APIs
constraints.card: All external internet connectivity and third-party API access become unavailable during the challenge. The application must continue its essential user journey using information and components available within the local environment.
product: The station edge node (on UPS power) runs grouping, scoring and seat allocation with no cloud dependency (local-first).
Passes are signed on the edge node and verified on driver handhelds with no network.
Riders without signal check in at kiosks or with staff tokens; Koottu still books a cab if any one phone in the group has signal.
Timetables, fleet registry and maps are cached locally; no maps API, no ride-hail API, no LLM.
sim: Madrid blackout scenario: the real 28 April 2025 blackout at 12:33. Left: a cloud-only coordinator collapses into free-for-all. Right: RAHA on the edge node keeps allocating.
Every 200-seed experiment sweeps phone reach 100%, 70%, 30% and 0%, comparing cloud and local architectures (Chennai and Madrid).
The simulator obeys the card too: three.js, fonts, maps and data are bundled; the EXTERNAL REQUESTS badge counts and blocks any outside call and stays at 0.

constraints.title: An API changes its response structure
constraints.card: A previously working API suddenly changes its response structure. A field may be renamed, moved into a nested object, change type, or become optional.
product: One adapter sits between every feed and the allocator: alias paths for renamed and nested fields, coercion for type changes, last-known-good and a local vehicle registry for missing fields.
Invariant checks catch semantic drift (same field, new meaning), such as an ETA that silently becomes epoch milliseconds or a capacity that becomes crush load.
Fail safe: if a seat count cannot be trusted, no passes are issued for that vehicle, so nobody is overbooked.
sim: Singapore line-closure scenario: the bus feed mutates at 10:30 mid-incident; pick any of six mutations (rename, nest, retype, optional, garbage, semantic) and watch both sides re-run live.
The JSON panel shows the real message, what a naive parser reads (NaN, a throw, a wrong count) and what RAHA's adapter reads.
Every mutation class is measured over 200 seeds, naive versus adapter (Chennai and Singapore): empty departures, turned away, worst wait.
